headline: FRANCHISE UPDATE (Hormuz by the Numbers) -- UKMTO confirmed 8 attacks in the Strait + 3 in the Arabian Gulf in the past week, 3
dek: [VERIFIED FACT -- UKMTO's own review] Reviewing the past week, UKMTO confirmed 8 attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and 3 in the Arabian Gulf. 3 affected vessels sank and 5 more had to be rescued.
sources: UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) weekly review + Lloyd's List Intelligence, via The National (UAE)
fault_line: Blockade working (Iran enforcing its lane, traffic at 20%) vs blockade failing (most tankers that try still get through under escort) -- the argument is over which number proves control.

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- UKMTO's own review] Reviewing the past week, UKMTO confirmed 8 attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and 3 in the Arabian Gulf. 3 affected vessels sank and 5 more had to be rescued. UKMTO said further incidents 'are known but cannot be independently verified.' [VERIFIED FACT -- traffic] Traffic in the Strait of Hormuz stands at about 20% of its prewar level, per Lloyd's List Intelligence figures cited by The National. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- IRGC] The IRGC claims at least 12 ships have caught fire since the start of the month, mostly after hitting naval mines -- unverified by UKMTO or other sources. [CONTEXT] UKMTO's two confirmed Nov 7-evening incidents (Warning 199-26 tanker fire off Khasab, crew evacuated; Warning 200-26 projectile strike on outbound tanker) were already recorded at 1000-03. No UKMTO or CENTCOM response yet to the Mehr claim of 4 tankers halted / 11 targeted in 10 days (1700-01, still HOLD). PORTWATCH: snapshot 2026-11-09 STILL STALE (latest observation Nov 1, 8-day lag; 7-day avg 4.43 transits/day vs 2025 baseline 85.53/day = 5.2%).
sections.what_verified: UKMTO (T1, primary source of the attack count) + The National (T2, reporting family) + Lloyd's List (T3, primary source of the traffic figure).
sections.what_disputed: RegionAlert/others report roughly 4 of 5 tankers attempt crossings successfully under escort or radar compliance -- the '20% of prewar traffic' (counted transits) and '80% cross successfully' (attempted crossings) measure different things and are not directly comparable; do not present them as contradicting each other. PortWatch's counted transits are stale (Nov 1) and cannot confirm the current level.
sections.why_matters: UKMTO's own count: 8 attacks in the Strait in one week, 3 ships sank -- and traffic is down to 20% of prewar. The counted numbers behind the blockade, not the claims.
sections.context: Background: FRANCHISE UPDATE (Hormuz by the Numbers) -- UKMTO confirmed 8 attacks in the Strait + 3 in the Arabian Gulf in the past week, 3 vessels sank, 5 rescued; Lloyd's List: Hormuz traffic ~20% of prewar level

totw_analysis: Our read: UKMTO's own count: 8 attacks in the Strait in one week, 3 ships sank -- and traffic is down to 20% of prewar. The counted numbers behind the blockade, not the claims. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Blockade working (Iran enforcing its lane, traffic at 20%) vs blockade failing (most tankers that try still get through under escort) -- the argument is over which number proves control.
